title: The serenity prayer
hookLine: Reinhold Niebuhr is credited with the prayer asking serenity, courage and wisdom

cards: It hangs on kitchen walls. It's printed on mugs and bookmarks and tucked into wallets. Some people can say it by heart without remembering where they learned it.
It's a short prayer, and its request is plain: serenity to accept the things that can't be changed, courage to change the things that can, and wisdom to know the difference.
The prayer is credited to Reinhold Niebuhr, an American preacher and theologian, and it has traveled a long way from any one pulpit since.

teach.h: LET IT GO, OR GET UP?
teach.b: Look at the shape of it. The first two requests pull in opposite directions. One says: let it go.
The other says: get up and do something. A person can lean too far either way, fighting what will never move, or shrugging at what could be fixed by Thursday. The prayer won't pick a side.
It asks for both, and then for the thing that decides between them. That last request is the hinge.

teach.h: IF ANY OF YOU LACK WISDOM.
teach.b: The letter of James says: "If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him."
Upbraideth not: in James's picture, God doesn't scold anyone for asking. The Gospels show both halves in a single night.

teach.h: NOT AS I WILL, BUT AS THOU WILT.
teach.b: In the garden of Gethsemane, Jesus prays: "O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt." He really asks, and he really yields.
Paul tells a smaller story about a thorn in the flesh.

teach.h: MY GRACE IS SUFFICIENT FOR THEE.
teach.b: He begged for it to be taken away, and the answer he heard was: "My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness." The letter never says the thorn left.
When he is weak, Paul goes on, then he is strong. So the serenity prayer isn't a shrug. Its last line asks for judgment, fresh each time: is this a wall to accept, or a door to push?
Some days the honest answer is, not sure yet. Which is exactly why the prayer asks for wisdom.

how: Some Christians pray the serenity prayer daily or keep it on a wall at home; it is also said aloud together in some recovery groups and other gatherings.

o: a monk's chant for clearing the mind of all worry
a calm-down slogan written for a greeting card
a prayer for serenity, courage and wisdom between them

games.q: the serenity prayer — tap the pairs.
p: to accept what can't be changed
not as I will, but as thou wilt

s: the serenity prayer asks only for calm acceptance
it asks for serenity and for courage, and then for the wisdom to tell which one a moment needs.
in Gethsemane, Jesus asks for the cup to pass before he yields
"let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt."
Paul's thorn in the flesh is taken away when he asks
he hears "my grace is sufficient for thee." the letter never says the thorn left.

games.q: you're Paul. something you call a thorn in the flesh won't go away. you've asked God to take it, and the answer is: my grace is sufficient for thee. what do you do?
o: accept it, and lean on that grace.
games.why: Paul says he will glory in his weaknesses instead, because God's strength is made perfect in weakness.

practice: Bring to mind one situation that's been sitting on your chest, and sort it gently: set down the part you can't change, the past, another person's choices, and hold up the part you can, even a little, a phone call, an apology, a first step.
If you pray, you can say the serenity prayer slowly, in the words you know, pausing after each line; if you don't, just let the sorting happen.

wordCard.voice: The serenity prayer. A short prayer credited to Reinhold Niebuhr, asking for serenity, for courage, and for the wisdom to tell which one this moment needs.

orig.note: Greek, James 1:5: wisdom. James says to ask God for it, who "upbraideth not."

carryVoice: Your line: know the difference. Serenity, courage, and the wisdom between them. See you tomorrow.
